Annual Crop Land: Annual Crop Land is a field of regularly spaced, low-growing plants such as wheat or corn, often arranged in straight, parallel rows.
Annual Crop Land shows uniform, recently tilled soil with visible seedbed patterns, unlike the undisturbed ground of Forest.
Annual Crop Land displays seasonal vegetation that is short and dense, contrasting with the tall, irregular canopy of Forest.
Annual Crop Land features geometrically precise field boundaries aligned with roads or irrigation channels, unlike the organic, winding edges of River.
Annual Crop Land has evenly colored, homogeneous plant cover at a consistent height, unlike the patchy, variable-height growth of Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Annual Crop Land lacks permanent woody structures like trees or vines, distinguishing it from Permanent Crop Land.
Annual Crop Land contains no built infrastructure such as rooftops or paved surfaces, unlike Residential Buildings or Industrial Buildings.
Annual Crop Land shows no linear, highly reflective asphalt or concrete strips, distinguishing it from Highway or Road.
Annual Crop Land exhibits rectangular or trapezoidal plots with sharp corners, unlike the irregular, meandering shape of River.
Annual Crop Land has no open water surface or specular reflections, setting it apart from Sea or Lake.
Annual Crop Land displays actively growing monoculture crops, unlike the mixed, non-cultivated grasses and forbs of Pasture Land.
Annual Crop Land is typically devoid of scattered trees or shrubs, unlike Forest which contains abundant woody vegetation.
Annual Crop Land shows evidence of recent mechanical cultivation such as furrows or ridges, absent in Permanent Crop Land.
Annual Crop Land lacks the clustered, irregular roof shapes and shadows characteristic of Residential Buildings.
Annual Crop Land has no industrial-scale storage tanks, smokestacks, or large flat-roofed structures seen in Industrial Buildings.
Annual Crop Land does not contain the sinuous, dark-blue water bodies or branching tributaries typical of River.
Annual Crop Land is flat or gently sloping with uniform elevation, unlike the steep, shaded slopes often found in Forest.
Annual Crop Land shows no shoreline features such as sandy beaches or rocky outcrops associated with Sea or Lake.
Annual Crop Land features repetitive, human-planned crop patterns, unlike the spontaneous, uneven growth of Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Annual Crop Land has no aquatic vegetation or emergent reeds along margins, distinguishing it from River and Sea or Lake.
Forest: Forest has dense, continuous tree canopy that blocks most ground visibility, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land which shows exposed soil or low-growing plants.
Forest contains tall, mature trees with visible trunks and branching canopies, unlike Annual Crop Land which displays uniform, low-height vegetation rows.
Forest features multi-layered vegetation including understory shrubs and ground cover, unlike Highway or Road which shows a smooth, linear, paved surface.
Forest exhibits high vertical structure with trees of varying heights, unlike Residential Buildings which show regularly spaced, rectangular, human-made structures with sharp edges.
Forest lacks geometric patterns or straight lines, unlike Industrial Buildings which display large, flat, angular roofs and repetitive architectural elements.
Forest has irregular, organic shapes and textures across its entire area, unlike Permanent Crop Land which often shows evenly spaced rows of orchard or vineyard trees.
Forest contains no visible man-made infrastructure such as roads or buildings, unlike Pasture Land which may include fences, barns, or grazing animals.
Forest shows minimal evidence of soil exposure or bare ground, unlike Annual Crop Land which frequently reveals tilled or harvested earth between crop rows.
Forest is dominated by woody perennial vegetation taller than 5 meters, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land whose plants are typically under 2 meters and non-woody.
Forest has deep green spectral signature in natural light due to broadleaf or conifer foliage, unlike Sea or Lake which reflects sky color and shows specular highlights.
Forest appears as a contiguous, textured mass without linear water features, unlike River which forms a narrow, sinuous, reflective corridor.
Forest lacks the open, grassy expanses and scattered livestock typical of Pasture Land.
Forest does not contain rooftop surfaces or solar panels visible at ground level, unlike Industrial Buildings which often feature large, unbroken roof planes.
Forest has no paved or gravel pathways, unlike Highway or Road which displays clearly defined, straight or gently curved transport corridors.
Forest shows no signs of residential density such as clustered houses, driveways, or street grids, unlike Residential Buildings.
Forest contains no cultivated fruit or nut trees arranged in regular spacing, unlike Permanent Crop Land which exhibits orchard-like uniformity.
Forest is not bounded by agricultural field margins or irrigation ditches, unlike Annual Crop Land which displays clear parcel boundaries.
Forest does not reflect sunlight as a continuous bright surface, unlike Sea or Lake which shows strong, cohesive mirror-like reflections.
Forest lacks the metallic or concrete textures and sharp shadows of Industrial Buildings.
Forest has no visible shoreline, wave action, or sediment plumes, unlike River which displays dynamic water flow and adjacent alluvial features.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land: Herbaceous Vegetation Land is dominated by low-growing non-woody plants such as grasses and forbs, unlike Forest which features tall, dense trees.

Herbaceous Vegetation Land shows continuous ground cover of green or brown grass-like vegetation without tree canopies, unlike Permanent Crop Land which contains regularly spaced rows of woody shrubs or vines.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land lacks the geometric patterns of plowed furrows or crop rows seen in Annual Crop Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land has no paved surfaces or linear infrastructure, distinguishing it from Highway or Road.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land contains no built structures, unlike Industrial Buildings or Residential Buildings.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land appears as open, relatively flat terrain covered in uniform low vegetation, unlike River which displays a narrow, sinuous, dark blue or gray water body.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land lacks the large, contiguous expanse of deep blue or reflective surface characteristic of Sea or Lake.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land does not show the patchy, irregular mosaic of grazed and ungrazed patches typical of Pasture Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land has no orchard-like spacing or trellis systems visible, unlike Permanent Crop Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land exhibits no signs of recent soil disturbance or bare earth strips common in Annual Crop Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land lacks the vertical structural complexity and shadow-casting canopy of Forest.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land shows no evidence of rooftop geometry, road networks, or building footprints found in Residential Buildings.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land contains no industrial-scale storage tanks, smokestacks, or large rectangular sheds like those in Industrial Buildings.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land has no linear, high-contrast edge between land and water like that defining River.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land does not display the wave patterns, coastal boundaries, or shoreline features of Sea or Lake.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land lacks the clustered, irregular arrangement of grazing animals often visible in Pasture Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land shows no irrigation ditches or drip-line patterns commonly associated with Permanent Crop Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land has no asphalt or concrete surfaces, lane markings, or vehicle tracks present in Highway or Road.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land contains no cultivated fruit trees, vineyards, or nut groves that define Permanent Crop Land.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land appears as uninterrupted, low-height vegetation cover without the scattered tree clumps sometimes seen at forest edges.
Highway or Road: Highway or Road is a long, straight or gently curving paved surface designed for vehicle travel, typically flanked by painted lane markings.
Highway or Road has multiple parallel lanes separated by painted lines, unlike River which flows in a single sinuous channel.
Highway or Road features engineered asphalt or concrete surfacing with visible texture and joint lines, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land which shows continuous plant cover.
Highway or Road displays consistent linear geometry with engineered curves and banking, unlike Sea or Lake which has an irregular, organic shoreline.
Highway or Road includes roadside infrastructure such as guardrails or concrete barriers, absent in Pasture Land.
Highway or Road shows tire wear patterns and longitudinal skid marks on its surface, unlike Residential Buildings which have vertical façades and windows.
Highway or Road is bordered by engineered shoulders—gravel or paved strips distinct from adjacent Forest.
Highway or Road contains embedded reflective pavement markers (cat's eyes) aligned along lane centers, not found in Annual Crop Land.
Highway or Road exhibits uniform width over extended distances, unlike River whose width varies naturally along its course.
Highway or Road has overhead signage mounted on metal poles, contrasting with Industrial Buildings which feature large windowless walls.
Highway or Road displays dashed or solid centerline markings dividing opposing traffic, unlike Permanent Crop Land which shows repetitive plant rows without artificial lines.
Highway or Road includes roadside drainage ditches or culverts, visually distinct from the natural water flow of a River.
Highway or Road shows parallel wheel ruts aligned with lane direction, unlike Forest where ground cover is uneven and unpatterned.
Highway or Road is flanked by standardized road-edge reflectors set at regular intervals, unlike Sea or Lake which lacks man-made linear markers.
Highway or Road features bridge abutments or overpass supports where it crosses other roads or railways, unlike Pasture Land which is uninterrupted open ground.
Highway or Road has clearly defined entry/exit ramps with tapered lane transitions, unlike Highway or Road itself—this distinguishes it from simple two-lane roads not classified as highways.
Highway or Road includes rumble strips along lane edges to alert drivers, absent in Residential Buildings.
Highway or Road shows utility poles aligned parallel to the direction of travel, unlike Industrial Buildings which cluster structures without linear pole alignment.
Highway or Road contains traffic islands or medians separating bidirectional flow, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land which lacks rigid geometric divisions.
Highway or Road displays road surface distress signs like cracks or potholes aligned along wheel paths, unlike River which shows smooth water surface or natural sediment patterns.
Industrial Buildings: Industrial Buildings have large, flat, corrugated metal roofs that are absent in Residential Buildings.
Industrial Buildings feature multiple tall smokestacks or ventilation towers not found in Annual Crop Land.
Industrial Buildings contain extensive networks of exposed pipes and ductwork unlike Forest.
Industrial Buildings display large loading docks with roll-up garage doors absent in Permanent Crop Land.
Industrial Buildings have wide, unbroken expanses of brick or concrete walls without windows, unlike Residential Buildings.
Industrial Buildings include overhead crane runways along their ceilings, which are missing in Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Industrial Buildings show clusters of industrial-scale air conditioning units on rooftops, unlike River.
Industrial Buildings have reinforced concrete foundations with visible anchor bolts, unlike Pasture Land.
Industrial Buildings contain large, segmented metal siding panels with repeating rivet patterns not seen in Sea or Lake.
Industrial Buildings exhibit rows of evenly spaced, high-mounted translucent roof panels for daylighting, unlike Highway or Road.
Industrial Buildings have massive sliding or bi-fold exterior doors designed for freight vehicles, unlike Forest.
Industrial Buildings feature prominent fire suppression piping mounted externally along walls, absent in Annual Crop Land.
Industrial Buildings include rooftop helipads or heavy-duty HVAC platforms not present in Residential Buildings.
Industrial Buildings display extensive chain-link fencing with industrial-grade gates, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Industrial Buildings have flat roofs with gravel ballast and numerous mechanical penthouses, unlike Permanent Crop Land.
Industrial Buildings contain large, rectangular exhaust fans mounted flush with roof edges, unlike River.
Industrial Buildings show evidence of chemical storage tanks or silos adjacent to structures, absent in Sea or Lake.
Industrial Buildings have wide-span truss roofs with exposed steel framing, unlike Pasture Land.
Industrial Buildings feature security lighting poles with industrial floodlights spaced at regular intervals, unlike Highway or Road.
Industrial Buildings include external staircases with grated metal treads and cage enclosures, not found in Residential Buildings.
Pasture Land: Pasture Land is a grassy area grazed by livestock, unlike Forest which is densely covered with trees.
Pasture Land features open, low-growing grasses with visible grazing animals, whereas Industrial Buildings contain large, solid-roofed structures.
Pasture Land shows uniform, short to medium-height vegetation maintained by herbivores, unlike Annual Crop Land which displays rows of cultivated plants or bare soil between crops.
Pasture Land lacks paved surfaces and linear infrastructure, distinguishing it from Highway or Road.
Pasture Land contains no permanent human dwellings, unlike Residential Buildings which show clustered houses with roofs and windows.
Pasture Land has no standing water bodies or visible shorelines, unlike River, Sea or Lake.
Pasture Land is dominated by living grasses rather than woody perennials, unlike Permanent Crop Land which includes orchards or vineyards with trellises or mature fruit trees.
Pasture Land appears as gently rolling or flat green terrain without tall vertical elements, unlike Forest which exhibits a high, closed canopy.
Pasture Land lacks the geometric patterns and seasonal bare patches of Annual Crop Land.
Pasture Land does not contain factory-like structures, smokestacks, or extensive paved yards, unlike Industrial Buildings.
Pasture Land shows no evidence of intensive irrigation infrastructure such as center-pivot sprinklers or drip lines, unlike many Permanent Crop Land plots.
Pasture Land is typically uninterrupted by asphalt or concrete lanes, unlike Highway or Road.
Pasture Land supports grazing animals but lacks the built environment of Residential Buildings, including driveways, fences, or sidewalks.
Pasture Land has no tree canopy coverage exceeding 10%, distinguishing it from Forest.
Pasture Land consists of herbaceous vegetation that regrows after grazing, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land which is often uncultivated, weedy, and ungrazed.
Pasture Land is managed for forage and shows signs of animal use like dung or worn paths, unlike Annual Crop Land which shows tillage marks or harvest residues.
Pasture Land lacks the dense, multi-layered understory and leaf litter typical of Forest.
Pasture Land contains no aquatic features or reflective water surfaces, unlike River, Sea or Lake.
Pasture Land is not subdivided into housing lots or marked by street grids, unlike Residential Buildings.
Pasture Land has no industrial-scale storage tanks, rail sidings, or loading docks, unlike Industrial Buildings.
Permanent Crop Land: Permanent Crop Land has regularly spaced, mature fruit or nut trees arranged in orderly rows, unlike Annual Crop Land which shows seasonal bare soil or young plants.
Permanent Crop Land features perennial woody plants with visible trunks and canopies that persist year-round, unlike Herbaceous Vegetation Land which consists of non-woody, seasonally dying plants.
Permanent Crop Land displays uniform, geometric tree canopies at consistent height and spacing, unlike Forest which has irregular, multi-layered, and uneven canopy heights.
Permanent Crop Land contains cultivated trees trained to low, manageable heights for harvesting, unlike Forest where trees grow tall and unpruned with natural branching patterns.
Permanent Crop Land shows clear, maintained ground cover between tree rows—often bare soil, mulch, or low grass—unlike Pasture Land which is densely covered with grazing-height grasses.
Permanent Crop Land lacks the dense, continuous green canopy of Forest and instead reveals significant gaps between individual tree crowns.

Permanent Crop Land has straight, parallel rows of trees aligned along agricultural infrastructure like drip lines or trellises, unlike Residential Buildings which contain clustered, irregularly shaped structures.
Permanent Crop Land exhibits no paved surfaces or vehicle access lanes wider than farm tracks, unlike Highway or Road which features continuous, wide, engineered asphalt or concrete surfaces.
Permanent Crop Land contains no rooftop structures or building footprints, distinguishing it from Industrial Buildings which show large, flat, angular roofs with ventilation units or loading docks.
Permanent Crop Land shows no water bodies within its boundaries, unlike River, Sea or Lake which display reflective, linear or expansive blue-gray surfaces.
Permanent Crop Land has no visible housing units, driveways, or street grids, unlike Residential Buildings which feature repeated small-scale architectural forms and paved local roads.
Permanent Crop Land lacks the fragmented, small-scale patchwork of varying crops seen in Annual Crop Land, instead maintaining consistent tree species across large contiguous areas.
Permanent Crop Land does not include grazing animals or hoof-printed soil, unlike Pasture Land which often shows signs of animal traffic and uneven vegetation height.
Permanent Crop Land has no industrial equipment such as cranes, smokestacks, or storage tanks, unlike Industrial Buildings which display prominent mechanical infrastructure.

Permanent Crop Land features tree rows oriented to maximize sun exposure, often aligned north-south, unlike Highway or Road which follows topographic or planning-based directional continuity regardless of aspect.
Permanent Crop Land shows no shoreline features like waves, sediment deposits, or aquatic vegetation, unlike River, Sea or Lake which exhibit distinct water-edge transitions.
Permanent Crop Land contains no intersecting paved streets or sidewalks, unlike Residential Buildings which display orthogonal or curvilinear road networks with curb edges.
Permanent Crop Land has no visible rooftops, windows, or architectural details, unlike Industrial Buildings which show large, repetitive structural elements like corrugated metal panels or skylights.

Permanent Crop Land maintains consistent tree density and spacing over hectares without abrupt transitions to built structures, unlike Residential Buildings which abruptly adjoin roads or open spaces.
Permanent Crop Land lacks the meandering, narrow, and sinuous shape of River, instead showing rigid, rectilinear field boundaries defined by tree rows.
Residential Buildings: Residential Buildings have multiple small, regularly spaced windows arranged in grid-like patterns on their façades.
Residential Buildings contain attached or detached dwellings with pitched or gabled roofs, unlike the flat or low-slope roofs typical of Industrial Buildings.
Residential Buildings feature front doors aligned with sidewalks and often include porches or stoops, distinguishing them from Highway or Road which lacks any enclosed structures.
Residential Buildings show visible domestic features such as mailboxes, house numbers, and garden fences, absent in Forest and Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Residential Buildings are arranged in repeating, human-scale blocks or rows, contrasting with the irregular, organic canopy coverage of Forest.
Residential Buildings include driveways or parking spaces directly adjacent to units, unlike River or Sea or Lake which contain no built infrastructure.
Residential Buildings display varied but modest architectural styles and colors, differing from the uniform, large-span metal or concrete exteriors of Industrial Buildings.
Residential Buildings often have small private yards or lawns immediately surrounding them, unlike Highway or Road which has no vegetation-integrated ground space.
Residential Buildings contain balconies or bay windows that project outward from walls, a feature not found in Annual Crop Land or Permanent Crop Land.
Residential Buildings show rooftop features like chimneys or solar panels, absent in Pasture Land and Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Residential Buildings are clustered at densities higher than Residential Buildings but lower than Industrial Buildings, and lack the open-field expanse of Pasture Land.
Residential Buildings have street-facing façades with symmetrical window-door arrangements, unlike the unbroken, windowless walls common in Industrial Buildings.
Residential Buildings include attached garages or carports integrated into the structure, unlike Highway or Road which contains only pavement and lane markings.
Residential Buildings exhibit clear separation between units via shared walls or narrow gaps, unlike the continuous canopy of Forest.
Residential Buildings feature roof overhangs extending beyond exterior walls, unlike the minimal or absent overhangs on Industrial Buildings.
Residential Buildings contain satellite dishes or exterior HVAC units mounted on walls or roofs, not present in River or Sea or Lake.
Residential Buildings show evidence of domestic maintenance such as trimmed hedges or potted plants, unlike the unmanaged growth in Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
Residential Buildings have multiple stories but rarely exceed five floors, distinguishing them from high-rise Industrial Buildings or dense urban cores not in this class list.
Residential Buildings include awnings above doors or windows, a detail absent in Annual Crop Land and Permanent Crop Land.
Residential Buildings display signage limited to names or numbers, unlike the large commercial lettering typical of Industrial Buildings.
River: River is a narrow, winding, linear body of flowing freshwater, typically bordered by natural banks, unlike the broad, still expanse of Sea or Lake.
River appears as a sinuous, dark-blue or grayish ribbon cutting through land, distinct from the irregular, textured patches of Forest or Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
River has a clearly defined, continuous channel with visible flow direction, unlike the static, unchannelled water surface of Sea or Lake.
River is flanked by gradual, natural slopes and often exhibits riparian vegetation, contrasting with the abrupt, engineered edges of Highway or Road.
River lacks the geometric regularity and straight segments typical of Highway or Road.
River shows meanders and bends at multiple scales, unlike the rigid, rectilinear layout of Residential Buildings or Industrial Buildings.
River is composed entirely of open water with no built structures on its surface, distinguishing it from Highway or Road which support vehicles and infrastructure.
River flows between two opposing landmasses without spanning them, unlike Highway or Road which connect separate areas across gaps.
River has variable width but maintains consistent linear continuity, unlike the fragmented, discontinuous shapes of Annual Crop Land or Permanent Crop Land.
River reflects sky and surrounding terrain dynamically, whereas Sea or Lake tends to show larger, more uniform reflections due to greater surface area.
River is rarely perfectly straight over distances longer than a few hundred meters, unlike the long, straight stretches common in Highway or Road.
River often displays visible current-induced ripples or surface texture, unlike the calm, glassy or wave-chopped surface of Sea or Lake.
River occupies a low-lying topographic corridor, contrasting with the elevated, flat-topped forms of Residential Buildings or Industrial Buildings.
River lacks the rectangular grid patterns and sharp angular boundaries seen in Residential Buildings or Industrial Buildings.
River is surrounded by natural or semi-natural land cover, not the uniform, human-planned layouts of Pasture Land or Annual Crop Land.
River does not contain regularly spaced rows of vegetation like Permanent Crop Land or Annual Crop Land.
River has no visible pavement, asphalt, or road markings, unlike Highway or Road.
River is not enclosed by walls or buildings, distinguishing it from the bounded, artificial spaces of Residential Buildings or Industrial Buildings.
River runs through varied terrain—valleys, plains, or gorges—unlike the flat, homogeneous expanses of Pasture Land or Herbaceous Vegetation Land.
River exhibits branching tributaries that converge, unlike the non-converging, parallel lanes typical of Highway or Road.
Sea or Lake: Sea or Lake is a large expanse of open water with no visible vegetation or built structures on its surface.
Sea or Lake has a smooth, reflective surface that mirrors the sky, unlike the textured, non-reflective surface of Forest.
Sea or Lake appears as a continuous blue or gray body of water with no discernible land boundaries within the frame, unlike River which follows a narrow, winding path.
Sea or Lake lacks linear infrastructure such as roads or highways crossing its surface, unlike Highway or Road which is defined by such features.
Sea or Lake contains no buildings—residential, industrial, or otherwise—whereas Residential Buildings and Industrial Buildings are characterized by clustered man-made structures.
Sea or Lake shows no evidence of agricultural patterns like rows of crops or field boundaries, unlike Annual Crop Land and Permanent Crop Land.
Sea or Lake has no grassy or shrubby vegetation cover visible at its surface, distinguishing it from Herbaceous Vegetation Land and Pasture Land.
Sea or Lake occupies a broad, unbroken area without the dendritic branching pattern typical of River.
Sea or Lake exhibits no shoreline vegetation bands or transitional zones with dense trees, unlike Forest which features continuous tree canopy extending to the edge.
Sea or Lake has no paved or gravel surfaces, unlike Highway or Road which displays clear linear, engineered surfacing.
Sea or Lake lacks the geometric grid patterns of cultivated fields seen in Annual Crop Land.
Sea or Lake shows no rooftops, walls, or architectural forms, unlike Residential Buildings and Industrial Buildings.
Sea or Lake does not contain livestock or grazing animals, unlike Pasture Land which often shows visible animals or fencing.
Sea or Lake has no orchard or vineyard layout of spaced woody plants, unlike Permanent Crop Land.
Sea or Lake displays no sediment-laden or turbid flow indicative of a flowing river channel, unlike River.
Sea or Lake has no adjacent transportation corridors such as highways running parallel to its edge, unlike Highway or Road which is inherently linear and transport-oriented.
Sea or Lake contains no harvested crop stubble or tilled soil patches, unlike Annual Crop Land which shows seasonal ground disturbance.
Sea or Lake lacks the patchwork mosaic of different land uses found in mixed urban-rural interfaces, unlike Residential Buildings which sit within structured, human-scaled layouts.
Sea or Lake shows no evidence of mining, storage tanks, or heavy machinery, unlike Industrial Buildings which feature prominent functional infrastructure.
Sea or Lake has no emergent vegetation such as reeds or cattails along its margins, unlike River which commonly displays riparian vegetation in narrow bands.
